prompt:
Summarize the following news article for an investor who follows Exxon Mobil (XOM).
Write a single paragraph of at most 100 words.

HEADLINE: UPDATE 2-Exxon signals fall in fourth-quarter upstream profit

BODY:
(Adds details in paragraphs 4 to 7)

Jan 7 (Reuters) - U.S. oil major Exxon Mobil said on Wednesday that lower crude oil prices could cut its fourth-quarter upstream earnings by about $800 million to $1.2 billion.

Oil prices declined 9.2% during the three months ended December 31, as concerns about oversupply and tariffs outweighed geopolitical risks.

Brent crude futures shed about 19% in 2025, the most substantial annual percentage decline since 2020 and their third straight year of losses, the longest such streak on record. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude logged an annual decline of almost 20%.

The company said in a regulatory filing that changes in gas prices could affect its quarterly upstream earnings from a negative $300 million to as much as a positive $100 million.

Exxon's snapshot is closely watched for clues on how the broader oil sector will fare when companies begin releasing quarterly results in a few weeks.

Analysts expect Exxon to report adjusted earnings of $1.66 per share for the fourth quarter, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company will release results for the final quarter of the year on January 30, the filing showed.

The energy major had posted $5.7 billion in upstream earnings for the third quarter. (Reporting by Pooja Menon in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar and Anil D'Silva)
text: Exxon Mobil flagged a potential $800 million–$1.2 billion drop in fourth-quarter upstream earnings due to a 9.2% decline in crude prices during Q4, part of a broader 2025 slump—Brent fell ~19% and WTI ~20%, marking a third straight annual loss, the longest streak on record. Gas price shifts could add a further swing of -$300 million to +$100 million. This follows Q3's $5.7 billion upstream earnings. Analysts expect adjusted EPS of $1.66 for Q4, with results due January 30. Exxon's disclosure is often viewed as an early indicator for sector-wide earnings trends amid ongoing oversupply and tariff-related pressures.
